sentences.show: 28 men were trapped in the Antarctic ice for almost two years. Not one of them died.
In December 1914, Ernest Shackleton sailed for Antarctica on a ship called Endurance. The plan: be the first to cross it on foot.
They never even landed. The sea froze around the ship, and held her like a fist.
For ten months, they drifted with the ice, through the polar winter.
Then the ice began to crush her. Shackleton gave the order: abandon ship.
A month later, they watched Endurance sink beneath the ice.
They camped on floating ice for five months, eating seals and penguins.
When the ice split under them, they rowed three lifeboats to a frozen rock called Elephant Island.
No one would ever look for them there. So Shackleton took five men and a seven-metre lifeboat, and sailed for help.
1,300 kilometres, across the worst ocean on Earth.
They hit South Georgia, on the wrong side. So three of them climbed across unmapped mountains for 36 hours, to a whaling station.
It took Shackleton four attempts to get back through the ice to Elephant Island.
On 30 August 1916, a Chilean tug reached them. Every single man was alive.
And in 2022, Endurance was found, 3 kilometres down, almost perfectly preserved.
Shackleton never gave up on his men. Don't give up on history. Subscribe.
